Subject: Pilot VPC deployment — request for MSA annex and audit window

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Vanguard Medical Group is interested in a scoped VPC/private deployment for our pilot (PHI in-scope). Before we proceed to procurement, our legal and security teams need two things: a draft addendum to the MSA that describes the VPC/on-prem boundary and operator access, and a checklist of evidence you accept for a pre-deployment audit (SOC 2 reports, operator attestation, KMS separation notes).

Can you share your proposed redlines for the MSA addendum and an audit checklist we can share with our compliance team? Also please confirm whether Redwood will accept a limited escrow-like proof-of-ability to provide operator access in an incident (we have outside counsel copied).

Target timeline: vendor selection call week of Apr 5 — can we get materials by Mar 31?

Thanks,
Grace Li
Director, IT Procurement
Vanguard Medical Group

Attachments: VMG-questions-audit-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), Procurement-RFP.pdf (referenced)

Hi Grace — thanks for the clear ask and the checklist.

Quick plan: I'll circulate a redline of the VPC/Private Deployment Annex (MSA addendum) this afternoon that addresses license boundary, operator access, and a narrow audit-evidence acceptance path. Neha (legal) will call out any clauses that need escalation to commercial/legal. Karthik (solutions) will add a short runbook excerpt for operator access controls and KMS handoff options.

Two clarifications that will help us scope the redline:
- Are you expecting unilateral on-site operator access, or a remote operator model with customer-managed jumpbox?
- Do you require escrow of any keys or just an attestable process and on-call access under NDA?

We intend to attach: MSA_VPC_Addendum_Redline_v1.docx and an audit-evidence checklist (spreadsheet) to the HubSpot deal (link below). Target to get materials to you by 2027-03-30 EOD PST to keep your timeline. If Baker & Co want to propose alternative wording, please send their markups and we will incorporate.

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot VPC deployment — request for MSA annex and audit window

Grace / Rishi — I reviewed the initial redline and the VMG checklist. High level comments (will send a tracked doc shortly):

1) License scope: we limit code/exec to the runtime artifacts necessary to serve inference. We cannot grant source/code escrow; recommend language that explicitly separates operator binaries from source and commits to an operator attestation protocol and a secure snapshot (hashes) delivered under NDA.

2) Audit window / evidence: we can accept SOC2 Type II report and selective supplemental evidence (operator access logs, KMS key policy excerpt, runbook excerpts). We cannot provide raw DB snapshots or PHI exports. Recommend the addendum include an "evidence matrix" table that enumerates acceptable docs and timelines for production audits (e.g., 10 business days to schedule, 30 business days to produce allowed evidence).

3) Operator access & escalation: rather than full-time on-site access, propose a model: remote operator with time-limited session recorded, customer-managed bastion, and a signed operator attestation post-maintenance. If VMG insists on on-site access, we need SLA/escort and limitations captured.

4) Escrow-like proof: we cannot do source-code escrow. We can provide an escrow-equivalent: notarized attestation and a compiled operator-only bundle in escrow that allows for incident response under defined triggers. That language requires legal sign-off and a commercial uplift; I flagged a permissive clause that limits its use to catastrophic incidents and requires a court/jurisdictional process.

I'll attach the tracked redline (MSA_VPC_Addendum_Redline_v2.docx) with inline suggestions and a short summary memo for execution. Please confirm whether Baker & Co will want to review separately.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachments: MSA_VPC_Addendum_Redline_v2.docx (tracked changes), evidence-matrix-template.xlsx

Neha / Rishi — thank you, this is very helpful and closer to what our security team needs. A couple of follow-ups:

- Our security lead prefers a documented escrow-equivalent rather than source escrow; your proposed operator-only bundle with restrictive triggers sounds workable — can you provide the exact suggested trigger language?
- SOC 2 Type II and the evidence matrix are acceptable. Can we confirm whether the 30 business day window you suggested is from formal notice or from scheduling? Our compliance will likely request formal notice.
- Baker & Co will send a few suggested edits to the operator access paragraph — copied.

If you can get the v2 redline and the evidence matrix uploaded to the HubSpot deal and to DocuSign (power-form link) today, procurement will circulate internally and we can lock the vendor selection call on Apr 5.

Best,
Grace
